A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 31-page versions of the same CAD-Llama study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAD generation, captioning, completion, and editing results, representation and pretraining ablations, and Fusion360 generalization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 3–6 and 8–9, together with qualitative demonstrations and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hierarchical annotation pipeline, SPCC representation, similarity-based grouping for pretraining, and LoRA instruction tuning. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepCAD for training and retain the same generation, captioning, completion, and editing tasks. Fusion360 evaluation already appears in v1 Appendix E.4; no coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same comparators: DeepCAD, SkexGen, and HNC-CAD for unconditional generation; GPT-4, GPT-3.5, LLaMA3, and Mistral for downstream tasks; and Text2CAD and CAD-Translator additionally for text-to-CAD. Newly cited CAD-MLLM and CAD-GPT are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, training settings, metrics, sample sizes, and two-shot baseline evaluation are unchanged. Section 4.2 still compares 9,000 generated models, sampled at 2,000 points each, against 3,000 test models. Appendix protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the code-format/hierarchical-description ablation in Table 6, in-context-pretraining ablation in Table 8, Fusion360 generalization analysis, and qualitative and failure examples. No supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 3 still reports CAD-Llama SR of 99.90%, Table 4 reports text-to-CAD accuracy of 84.72%, and Table 9 reports Fusion360 accuracy of 78.35%. Rankings and findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The CAD/SPCC definitions, annotation mappings, cosine similarity, and training objectives in Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Appendix definitions also match, with no added or revised theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical annotation, adaptive pretraining, instruction tuning, and CAD-generation performance. The related-work addition does not revise these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hierarchical descriptions, code formatting, pretraining, and generalization remain unchanged. Appendix E.6 and Figure 25 retain the same limitations involving parameter errors and mismatches between text instructions and generated CAD models.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices provide the same optimizer, context lengths, LoRA settings, hardware and training costs, quantization details, and prompts. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CAD-MLLM and CAD-GPT, briefly describing their multimodal inputs and spatial-reasoning capabilities, with corresponding bibliography entries. This modestly expands coverage of closely related research; other references match after renumbering.

P1.justification: The related-work paragraph receives a short insertion about CAD-MLLM and CAD-GPT. Section organization and the remaining prose are retained, apart from citation updates and resulting line and page breaks.

P2.justification: Figures, table contents, captions, and numbering are retained. Limited layout reflow moves Table 4 lower on page 7 and carries the conclusion's final line and acknowledgment onto page 9. Supplementary example pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a limited literature omission by acknowledging CAD-MLLM and CAD-GPT and describing their relevant capabilities in Section 2. This makes the scholarly context more complete. The overall gain is small because the methods, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
